back: Average reward, response length, advantage std (mean must be ~0), entropy, held-out accuracy; the raw loss is not a progress meter.
H = -sum_v p_v log p_v, from 0 (one certain token) to log V (uniform); averaged over generated tokens for monitoring.

front: Advantage std as a health signal
back: About 1 is a good scale; far below 1 is a vanishing signal (rewards collapsing), far above 1 gives spiky updates; 0 means no signal.
The sequence ratio is exp of a SUM of token log-ratios, so it drifts with length; exp(sum/L) keeps the ratio comparable across lengths (GSPO).
Asymmetric clipping, eps_high > eps_low (e.g. 0.28 vs 0.2), so positive-advantage tokens can keep gaining probability.
Drop prompts whose rollouts all have the same reward and sample new ones, so every batch has non-zero advantages.
Sequence sum: A_i/G per token; sequence mean: A_i/(G L_i); token mean (DAPO): A_i / sum_j L_j.
Each rollout gets the same total push, so per-token weight falls with length: long wrong rollouts are under-penalised per token.
Dividing by sigma flattens weights across difficulty (sum|A| 4.95 vs 7.48 for k=1, 4 of 8 versus 1.75 vs 4.0 without). Dr. GRPO removes it; DeepSeek V3.2 keeps it.

front: Why KL on summed log-probs misbehaves
back: The KL term scales with length, encouraging long outputs, and once rewards collapse it is the only gradient; common advice for math is no KL.
Hard: SFT on the teacher's text (no logits needed). Soft: match the teacher's token distribution with KL (needs logits and a shared tokenizer). Combined: CE + lambda * KL.
Mean cross-entropy over answer tokens only; row t predicts token t+1, answer rows are prompt_len-1 .. L-2; equals the negative average log-probability.
Chat-templated prompt ids + '<think>thinking</think>\n\ncontent' ids + EOS, keep prompt_len, filter by max length, hold out a small validation split.
An extension to the book's length filter: keep only traces whose final answer is verified correct and non-empty; less data, fewer taught mistakes.
Batching raises throughput, not latency. Generation pads on the left with an attention mask (True = pad); sorting by length reduces padding waste.
